description:
Review of wave 1 (spec v5d, confirmed by running): native kernels disagree with Elixir mode (which is normative). (1) mixed i64/f64 comparisons convert the integer to double: 9007199254740993 == 9007199254740992.0 is true natively, false in Elixir; i64_max < 9.223372036854776e18 is false natively, true in Elixir. Compare exactly (Erlang compares int vs float by exact value). (2) min/max on signed zeros: min(-0.0, 0.0) is 0.0 natively, -0.0 in Elixir mode (Erlang returns the first argument when they compare equal); max and the other order too. Check Erlang's exact rules in Lab/beam/otp before coding.

Done when tests compare native and __defk_elixir__ on these inputs (incl. ===, <, <=, >, >=, ==, != at 2^53+-1, i64 min/max vs their nearest doubles, NaN-free) and min/max on +-0.0 in both orders, with no measurable cost on the catalog kernels (check dot/geo_nearest generated C still vectorises where it did).
title: Native comparisons and min/max must agree with Elixir (mixed i64/f64, signed zeros)
